title: Incident runloop, responder decision canvas, and communication stencils
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a single, repeatable incident runloop used by responders at Redwood Inference, describes a lightweight decision canvas for triage, includes canonical runbook fragments for frequent failure modes, and provides approved communication stencils for internal status and customer-facing notices. The goal is consistent, fast decisions that preserve customer trust while minimizing operational churn.

Scope
-----
- Applies to production incidents affecting hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control-plane services.
- Focused on availability degradations, latency regressions, model-quality regressions, billing anomalies, and infrastructure capacity events.
- Not intended for purely engineering RFCs or pre-prod issues.

Who owns this doc
------------------
- Document owner: eng-sre (oncall team)
- Primary contacts: oncall-rotation@redwood.ai, eng-sre-runbooks@redwood.ai

Quick links
-----------
- Slack channel: #incidents (primary bridge)
- Pager: PagerDuty service: REDWOOD-PROD
- Status page template: status.redwood.ai/template/incident-stub

Incident lifecycle (single runloop)
----------------------------------
1) Detect (automated signal or human report)
   - Source examples: SLO alerts (prometheus), error budget burn, customer ticket, external status page ping.
   - Action: declare incident severity using thresholds below and notify the oncall.

2) Triage (5–15 minutes)
   - Use the Decision Canvas (below) to gather facts.
   - Decide initial containment step(s) and scope of impact (customers, regions, models).

3) Contain (15–60 minutes)
   - Execute fast mitigations (auto-fallback to smaller model variants, scale up dedicated pool, block noisy tenant).
   - If user-facing impact: post initial status update (internal and public).

4) Mitigate & Repair (hours)
   - Apply durable fixes, coordination with infra/product/legal as needed.
   - Track actions in the incident timeline.

5) Recover & Validate (end of hours)
   - Verify SLOs returning to baseline over at least two rolling windows (P95, P99).

6) Postmortem (within 72 hours: draft; within 7 days: publish)
   - Author a blameless postmortem using template in this doc.

Decision canvas (triage checklist)
---------------------------------
- Title: One-line symptom description.
- Time window: when did it start (UTC).
- Signals: top 3 metrics affected (e.g., API errors, request latency P95, GPU utilization).
- Blast radius: percentage of customers/regions/models affected.
- User impact: severity_level = {SEV1|SEV2|SEV3} (guideline below).
- Quick hypothesis: most-likely cause and immediate test to confirm.
- Containment options (pick 1–2): rollback, autoscale up, route traffic to fallback region, reduce concurrency, enable degraded-mode.
- Owner & next checkpoint (time).

Severity guidelines
-------------------
- SEV1 (Critical): Total service outage or >50% customers seriously impacted, business-critical features non-functional. Pager oncall + SRE lead + Eng manager.
- SEV2 (High): Partial degradation with clear workaround, significant latency regressions for a subset of customers. Pager oncall + SRE oncall.
- SEV3 (Low): Cosmetic errors, minor throttling, single-customer impact with mitigation in place. Notify oncall queue asynchronously.

Escalation matrix (text table)
-----------------------------
Role | Primary contact | Escalation window
------|-----------------|------------------
Oncall responder | oncall-rotation@redwood.ai | immediate (pager)
SRE lead | liam.chen@redwood.ai | 15 minutes for SEV1
Platform eng manager | sofia.martinez@redwood.ai | 30 minutes for ongoing SEV1s
Director of Operations | rajiv.kapoor@redwood.ai | 60+ minutes if impact not contained
Customer success lead | cs-ops@redwood.ai | notify within 30 minutes of customer-facing impact

Canonical runbook fragments (copy these into service runbooks)
------------------------------------------------------------
1) High API latency (P95 > 300ms for >=5m)\   
- Decision canvas: confirm increased queue length on frontend, check model latency per-variant.
- Quick checks:
  - kubectl -n prod get pods | grep frontend
  - curl https://internal-metrics/serving/p95?window=5m
- Fast mitigations:
  - Scale frontend: terraform apply -var='scale_frontend=+20' modules/frontend
  - Enable token-level caching: POST /admin/cache/enable?prefix_weights=0.5
  - Failover heavy models: route heavy-model -> heavy-model-quantized
- Longer fix: tune batching config, raise worker replica count, investigate kernel-level perf with nvprof.

2) Model-quality regression (sudden accuracy drop on eval set)
- Decision canvas: confirm eval loss trending and customer complaints.
- Quick checks:
  - curl -s https://eval-api/redwood/model-<id>/latest-metrics | jq .
  - check rollout logs: gsutil cat gs://rollout-logs/model-<id>/recent.json
- Fast mitigations:
  - Pin traffic to previous model version: PATCH /api/rollouts/traffic -> {"model":"v1.2.3","percent":100}
  - Pause automatic canary promotion: PATCH /api/rollouts/<id>/pause
- Longer fix: revert problematic changes, run targeted evals, update prompts, re-run calibration.

3) Noisy-tenant causing capacity exhaustion
- Decision canvas: isolate based on tenant_id high token usage.
- Quick checks:
  - SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) FROM telemetry WHERE ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum desc LIMIT 10;
- Fast mitigations:
  - Apply rate limit: PATCH /api/tenants/<id>/limits -> {"qps": 20}
  - Migrate noisy tenant to burst-only pool or throttle background jobs.

Postmortem template (must be used for SEV1/SEV2)
--------------------------------------------------
- Title (one line)
- Date and incident id
- Severity
- Summary (2–3 sentences)
- Timeline (chronological bullets with timestamps UTC)
- Root cause analysis (why the bug/incident happened)
- Detection gap (how it was detected and why not earlier)
- Remediation / mitigation taken during incident
- Permanent fixes (code/config/ops)
- Action items (owner, due date, status)
- Customer impact (affected customers, duration, credits if applicable)
- Lessons learned and follow-up improvements
- Link to runbook(s) and relevant PRs/rollouts

On-call rotation policy and sample cadence
----------------------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week primary, 1 week secondary for SRE oncall.
- Handoff window: daily 09:00 UTC overlap and formal handoff doc in #oncall-handoffs.
- Escalation backup: each schedule entry must list first escalation and manager backup.
- OOO coverage: fill shifts in the oncall calendar 2 weeks in advance or assign a buddy.
- Compensation: per People Ops policy.

Game day program (quarterly)
----------------------------
Objective: validate the runloop, test cross-team communication, and surface brittle automations.
Structure:
- Prebrief (15m): goals, safety rails, scope, and opt-out list.
- Injector tasks (2–4): e.g., region throttling, model rollback, CSI storage failure simulations.
- Live exercise (60–90m): responders follow runloop, communicate to status page, execute mitigations.
- Debrief (30m): capture timeline, identify gaps, assign action items.
Scoring rubric:
- Detection time (target <5m): 25 points
- Containment time (target <30m): 25 points
- Communication clarity (internal & external templates used): 20 points
- Root cause identified and action items created: 20 points
- Postgame documentation published: 10 points

Status page and customer comms templates
--------------------------------------
Public status template (initial notice):
- Title: [Service] Degraded - [short symptom]
- Impact: We are investigating an issue affecting [subset/all] customers in [region(s)].
- Start time: 2026-02-14T14:12:00Z
- Next update: in 30 minutes
- What we are doing: We are actively routing traffic to fallback clusters and limiting concurrent model requests while we investigate.
- Link: status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-20260214-01

Internal status bulletin (for execs / CS):
- Subject: Incident INC-20260214-01 — SEV1 — Short summary
- Body: One-line impact, current measurables (error-rate, SLO delta), remediation actions, named owners, ETA for next update. Attach recent graphs (P95, error rate).

Customer email template (when >1 customer affected / >1h)
Subject: Important update: temporary service degradation
Body:
Hello {customer_name},

We are currently investigating a service degradation that may affect {affected_feature}. Our engineers have identified that {brief finding} and have taken {mitigation}. We expect a fix or meaningful update by {ETA}. We will notify you again by {time}.

If you are seeing increased errors, you can mitigate by {workaround}. We apologize for the disruption and will share a post-incident summary when available.

— Redwood Inference Support

Playbook hygiene and runbook governance
--------------------------------------
- Every runbook referenced in an incident must be reviewed after the incident and, if changed, the PR must reference the incident id.
- Runbooks have an annual TTL review; owners receive automated reminders 30 days before expiry.
- Runbook changes require at least one reviewer from another team (cross-review).

Reporting & KPIs for the oncall program
-------------------------------------
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target: < 2 minutes for SEV1
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) target: < 45 minutes for SEV1
- Postmortem coverage: 100% for SEV1, 75% for SEV2
- Game day cadence: quarterly with >80% attendance from responders

Appendices
---------
A. Slack templates (copy/paste)
- Internal quick update: "INC-20260214-01 | SEV1 | Investigating increased 5xxs in us-west. Owner: @aisha. Initial mitigation: throttled tenant X. Next update in 20m."
- Bridge join instruction: "Join Zoom bridge: zoom.us/j/xxxxx, PIN: 12345"

B. Example CLI snippets
- scale workers:
```bash
terraform apply -var=\"worker_count=+10\" modules/serving
```
- revert rollout (example):
```bash
curl -X PATCH -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts/abc123 -d '{"target_version":"v1.2.2"}'
```

C. Post-incident checklist (7 days)
- Draft postmortem (72h)
- Publish postmortem (7d)
- Close action items or convert to backlog tickets (14d follow-up)
- Runbook updates completed and reviewed (14d)

If you have questions or want this injected into a team runbook, contact eng-sre-runbooks@redwood.ai.
